leading_positions.synthesis: Six of eight members put B051 in their preferred configuration, all with the same two laureates (Hidetoshi Katori and Jun Ye). They differ on the rest of the prize and on the citation wording: Danielsson and Pearce pair it with B009, while Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson list B051 alone. The citations stress different things: the 10^-18 accuracy level (Danielsson, Lindroth, Olsson), magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms (Johansson), or a new regime of time and frequency precision (Kroll). Even the supporters attach reservations about novelty against the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, the unfinished SI redefinition of the second, and whether Lemonde and others are left out. Olsson also doubts whether Ye's credit is for invention or for later records.

Two members, Danielsson and Pearce, prefer a two-part prize of IceCube (Francis Halzen alone) and lattice clocks (Katori and Ye). Both flag a single-name credit for a large collaboration, with DUMAND, Baikal and AMANDA as precursors, as the main weakness of the B009 part. Both also say the pairing could look like a convenience pairing of unrelated physics. Pearce has professional familiarity with astroparticle physics and the chair therefore counts himself as a possibly non-neutral reader of B009. Kroll and Olsson raised the B009 pairing only as a question or not at all; they do not list it as preferred.

Eriksson alone prefers B050 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) as a single-part prize, citing a theory-plus-experiment story and mature, stable recognition. B050 is also named as an alternative by seven members (Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce), so it is the most widely named fallback although it is the first choice of only one member. The recurring objection, raised by Eriksson himself and by Danielsson, Olsson and Pearce, is that Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang sit outside the credited names, together with partial coverage of three-dimensional topological insulators and the 2016 topology prize.

Mehlig alone prefers B027 (Bloch, Greiner, Zoller) for ultracold-atom quantum simulation, with B050 and B051 as alternatives. Lindroth lists B027 as an alternative. The credited set has five names, so any three-person prize leaves out Cirac or Dalibard, and Jaksch is not on the list; Mehlig calls the set a judgement rather than settled history and calls the case less crisp than B050 or B051.

areas_of_agreement: B051 is the most widely preferred item: six of eight members explicitly list it, and all six credit the same two laureates, Katori and Ye.

Every member who addresses the performance of optical lattice clocks accepts that the 10^-18 level is established and reproduced independently; the doubts concern novelty relative to earlier prizes, not whether the measurements are sound.

Members who discuss B050 (Eriksson, Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce) name it as a preferred or alternative item and agree that the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang omission is the central open attribution question.

Several members (Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce) say they rely on memory or on colleagues for priority histories and would accept an outside expert report or archival check before a final decision.
No member reports a conflict that requires recusal from B051 or B050.
scientific_disputes: Whether the lattice clock is a distinct achievement or the next step in a line already recognised by the 2005 (frequency comb) and 2012 (ion control) prizes. Lindroth locates the distinct step in simultaneous interrogation of many atoms at the magic wavelength; Kroll, Johansson, Danielsson, Mehlig and Olsson raise the overlap as an objection.
Whether a thematic two-part prize (B009 with B051) is better than a single-achievement prize such as B050. Danielsson and Pearce both note that B050 alone could be the cleaner prize.

Whether the IceCube result should be cited for the 2013 diffuse flux only, as Pearce says he would do in reply to Danielsson, or also for source associations such as TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068 and the Galactic plane, where the significance is described as still moderate or not independently checked.

Whether B050 and B027 are mainly conceptual or platform achievements and whether a lack of applications matters; Eriksson accepts that B050 rests on conceptual impact, and Mehlig notes that the promised solution of classically intractable problems is only partly delivered for B027.
Whether the 2016 topological-phase prize makes B050 look like a second prize for the same theme.
attribution_disputes: B051: whether Katori and Ye are the right two names. Lindroth, Johansson, Kroll and Olsson mention Lemonde and others (Ludlow, Hinkley, Bloom, Derevianko, Takamoto) as possibly decisive. Olsson asks whether Ye's credit is for the original invention or for later accuracy and many-body records, and whether Katori alone is defensible.

B009: whether Halzen alone can be defended for a collaboration of hundreds with unlisted instrument builders, analysis leads and precursor projects (DUMAND, Baikal, AMANDA). Danielsson and Pearce, the two members who list it, both flag this, and Pearce says he cannot resolve it from the supplied credit.

B050: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed HgTe, which Molenkamp tested, and are not among the credited names; the three-dimensional work (Fu-Kane-Mele, Moore-Balents, Hasan, Cava) is also only partly covered.
B027: any three of Bloch, Greiner, Zoller, Cirac and Dalibard leave out someone, and Jaksch is unlisted.

B038: with four credited names any three-person prize leaves out Blais or Girvin or an experimentalist, which Johansson and Pearce both note; Pearce asks Johansson whether he prefers Wallraff or Girvin in a trio.
maturity_disputes: B051: the SI second has not been redefined, so some of the impact is prospective. Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce each raise this. Lindroth asks whether to wait; Lindroth argues cross-continent clock comparisons already provide independent confirmation.

B009: the 2013 diffuse flux is described by supporters as confirmed in several channels, but source identification is still partial; Pearce says he has not verified the current significance of NGC 1068 and Galactic-plane results.
B038: Johansson and Pearce both question whether the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits makes a circuit QED prize premature this year.
B050: Eriksson and others treat it as mature and overdue; the counter-view is the 2016 topology prize and the absence of applications.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson directs the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology, whose programme is built on circuit QED (B038), and would recuse himself from any decision on B038; he has moved it to an alternative.

Kroll's PhD included a stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, and JILA is Ye's institution; Kroll calls this a distant mentor-lineage link that does not appear to require recusal. Kroll also notes a WACQT institutional link to Chalmers (Johansson's base), not tied to a specific candidate, and subject adjacency to B033 and B038.

Lindroth is a long-time collaborator of Anne L'Huillier and attosecond groups; she says this does not concern B051 and does not require recusal, but she asks colleagues to challenge possible sympathy for atomic-physics candidates.

Pearce (chair) works in PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur and has professional familiarity with IceCube-adjacent astroparticle physics but no known tie to Halzen; he lists B009 in his own configuration and says he may be a stronger advocate than a neutral reader.

Olsson shares a department-level affiliation with Johansson at Chalmers, who has disclosed a stake in B038, and would not recuse on any shortlisted candidate; Mehlig notes general institutional proximity to Johansson and Olsson in the Gothenburg environment, relevant if B038 or B033 is considered.
Danielsson and Eriksson report no specific conflict; Eriksson notes only that his own electronic-structure theory work is close in field to B050 and B002.
questions_for_round2: B051: Is the lattice clock a distinct achievement from the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and if so should the citation name the simultaneous interrogation of many atoms at the magic wavelength (as Lindroth suggests) and not general clock accuracy?

B051: Does the priority record for the 2001-2003 magic-wavelength lattice proposals (including Lemonde and others) and for the first lattice clocks support exactly Katori and Ye, and is Ye credited for invention, for accuracy and stability records, or for the many-body clock?
B051: Should the committee wait for the redefinition of the SI second, or is the independently reproduced 10^-18 performance a sufficient basis now?

B009: Can a one-person IceCube credit for Halzen be defended against the collaboration, instrument builders and precursor projects, and is an outside expert report needed? Should the citation be restricted to the 2013 diffuse flux?

Do members prefer a two-part prize with unrelated physics (B009 with B051) or a single-achievement prize such as B050 or B051 alone, and what would make the pairing a scientific judgement rather than a convenience?

B050: Can Kane, Mele and Molenkamp be credited fairly without Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and does the 2016 topology prize weigh against it? Would Eriksson support B051 or a B050 plus B051 prize if the credit question is not settled?
Do Mehlig, Eriksson and the other members who rely on memory for B027 or B050 priority histories want an outside expert report requested before the final ballot?
B038: Given Johansson's disclosed recusal and the 2025 prize, should B038 be treated as a live candidate in round 2 or set aside?
summary.chair_observation: On the explicit round-1 files, B051 is the only item preferred by more than two members (six of eight), B009 is preferred by two as a second part, and B050 and B027 are each preferred by one member, with B050 named as an alternative by seven. Preference counts do not settle the open questions, since every member who prefers B051 also records novelty, priority or timing doubts, and the two members who prefer a B009 part both say the single-name credit is unresolved. Round 2 should concentrate on the credit questions for B051, B009 and B050 rather than on counts.
